data.narrative:
AlixLabs, a Series A semiconductor chip company founded by Jonas Sundqvist, Dmitry Suyatin, and Amin Karimi, has raised €15M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 8 private and 3 public comparables in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, including same-stage private peers Rebellions ($2.3B), d-Matrix ($2.0B), and adjacent-stage Positron AI ($1.0B), alongside public anchors ALAB, NVDA, and AMD.

Two triangulation methods prove applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using the €15M total raised as a proxy base and applying a typical 2.0x Series A step-up multiplier, implies a valuation of €30M. Peer-median analysis across the three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of €2.0B, with a range of €1.0B to €2.3B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied absent disclosed revenue figures. The wide dispersion between these two methods reflects stage-maturity variance within the peer set.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of €26M to €2.3B, with a median estimate of €1.0B. The primary uncertainty stems from AlixLabs' revenue traction and product commercialization velocity relative to higher-valued peers. Stage-progression implies the lower bound; peer positioning suggests values clustered toward the €1.0B–€2.0B range if the company demonstrates competitive technical or market differentiation comparable to Rebellions or d-Matrix.
